newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait to open market to private Internet supplier.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait to open market to private Internet supplier.

text.p: Kuwait plans to open the local market to private Internet suppliers, a move which could cut fees by 90 percent, a newspaper reported on Monday.
The Ministry of Communications "will lift restrictions on firms (providing Internet) to allow them to set the charge," al- Qabas daily quoted undersecretary Salman al-Roumi as saying.
"Big competition will reduce the Internet fee to the lowest level and could drop to five dinars ($16.6)," Roumi added without giving a date for the move.
Individual Internet users in Kuwait, which has a population of about two million, currently pay 60 dinars per month while firms pay 95 dinars for the service.

GULFNET International -- under the name of Kuwait Electronic Messaging Services -- says it currently provides the Internet service in Kuwait under the authority of the Ministry of Communications. Another firm, GulfNet Kuwait, claims to be the sole provider according to a contract with the ministry.
